steps.note: S2.2.1.2 states that the first rows remove the effect of the unknown scratch contents, the middle rows add the contribution and the last rows restore the scratch values, so the net target change is independent of the initial scratch values; the explicit expression (JV+RG)x is not written, but the cancellation mechanism is.
S2.2.1.3 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2 with the side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, and S2.2.1 gives net coefficient 1 for T=S.
S2.2.1.3 gives the complex-case central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 with the side wires cancelling the intersection-zero and intersection-two cases.
S2.2.1.4 gives forward, inverse, forward stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), and S2.2.1.2 gives the schedule that restores the scratch values in each invocation.
The S2.2.3 method says to tabulate the orthogonal residual of every edge, and S2.2.3.7 says edges join comparable labels, but the per-edge residuals and their dimensions are never given.
The plan states that neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal (S2.2.3.2), but it never treats the side edge 2->5, the inclusion <t_X> in t_Y^perp, or the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2.

The plan states that the only decreasing edges are the central 3->4 edges, each losing h, that sources sum to N and sinks to Wm-N, that gate contributions cancel to give a signed total Wm-2N, and that L=Ich gives an absolute total Wm-2N+2L.

S2.2.3.9 states that over F_2 a nondegenerate space is nonalternating exactly when it has a norm-one vector, that each nonzero residual has one, and so has an orthonormal basis; the plane-absorption argument is not spelled out.
S2.2.3.10 gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.

S2.2.5.2 gives weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors, and the S2.2.5 method and S2.2.5.3 split the phase difference of nested labels into one coefficient wt(v) per residual basis vector; the explicit sum formula is not displayed.
S2.2.5.3 gives that wt(v) is odd, so the phase coefficient is +-1 mod 4, and S2.2.5.4 uses H diag(1,-1) H = X to turn the character into X_v, giving aI+bX_v or its inverse.
S2.2.5.5 states that each residual vector contributes one factor acting on all k columns (a k-th tensor power), and S2.2.5.1 gives s_c factors in total.

The plan gives the exceptional pair X_a->Y_a with C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), the repair by Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after via C=iZC^{-1}Z, and the negation of the X outputs; that the zero label has frame I and the full label C^{otimes m} is not stated explicitly.
The plan states L/N<1/2, the deficit N-2L_b>0 giving s_b<W_b m, and the complex deficit 2N-2L_c>0.
The value eta_b=339/22587335000000 appears nowhere in the plan; S2.2.6 only says the deficits exceed 20*2^{-50}.
The value eta_c=73/19906842167500 appears nowhere in the plan.
S2.2.6 states that both deficits exceed 20*2^{-50} and m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50}), so s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}; the justification log m<20 is not stated.

S3.1 states the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones in Pi, but none of the elimination proof (the pivot at the rightmost entry of the topmost nonzero row, lower-triangular clearing, repetition on active indices).
The plan works over Z/q^bZ, but it never chooses a fixed odd prime avoiding the denominators of a finite factor table so that the identities specialize with invertible triangular factors.

S3.2 and S3.2.1 assert that the triangular transforms cost O(V) by controlled shifts, but never say that coordinates are updated in descending physical order so that earlier coordinates keep their original values.
S3.2.2 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, the interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j, sending (h,d) to (h+d,d), and S3.2.3 gives one interchange per one of Pi, a in all.
S4.9 gives E=64(W+m+1)^3 and implicitly B=s+E, and S7.1.1 gives C_1=20, but nu, C_0=128mB^2, Delta and the rule C_1=max{20,nu+3} are never defined.
S4.9 states the chain recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E with E=64(W+m+1)^3 at internal nodes and A(e)<=8e at leaves; the gate count showing that one invocation stays below E is not spelled out.
S4.9 gives sx+E<=(s+E)x and asserts A(e)<=8B^2d^{nu+1} and the C_0d^{C_1} total, but omits the unrolling step B^{k+1}<=B^2d^nu (from k<=ceil(log_m d) and B<=m^nu) that produces the d^nu factor.

S4.9 only says 'at most C_0d^{C_1} fractional and integer bits, which is o(p)'; it omits the induction that depth ell gives values in 2^{-(p+ell)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^ell, the p+Delta / Delta+3 reservation, and the condition epsilon*C_1<1.
S4.10 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so the result stays in the disk and the truncation error is below sqrt2 2^{-p}.

summary: P02 covers the bank-exchange network (4/4) and the complex phase interface (4/4) in full. It covers the label budget only at the level of telescoping, the nonalternating criterion and the loss ratios (3/5, with no residual table and no side-edge 2->5 argument). For the rank saving it has the deficit and exponent argument but not the exact eta values (2/4). For the matrix shear it has only the one-interchange implementation (1/4: no elimination proof, prime choice or descending-order update). For the simultaneous layer it has only the depth recurrence and the row-sum truncation (2/5: no constants, no unrolling to B^2d^nu, no bit-reservation argument). Total 16 of 26 present, none wrong.
